newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Samsung agrees Fokker takeover terms - Dutch TV.
newsitem.headline: Samsung agrees Fokker takeover terms - Dutch TV.

text.p: Negotiators from Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries have reached broad agreement on a takeover of bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker NV, Dutch television news said on Sunday evening.

Dutch television said the Samsung negotiators, the Dutch government and the administrators appointed to run the bankrupt company had set out broad terms for a takeover of Fokker in a memorandum of understanding drawn up on Friday.
Samsung's senior management was expected to decide by Tuesday whether to approve these terms and if they did, a final agreement was expected by Friday, Dutch television said.
The television broadcast did not include any direct comment from representatives of Samsung Aerospace, the Dutch government, or Fokker's administrators.
Fokker was declared bankrupt on March 15 after majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace cut off financial aid, saying it was no longer able to bear Fokker's huge losses.
Since then Samsung Aerospace has emerged as the only serious candidate to revive Fokker's core plane-making operations.
In September the administrators gave Samsung the exclusive right to examine Fokker's books with a view to a possible takeover bid. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
